subject: Post-call: Searchly evaluation pack + recommended next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@searchly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Searchly evaluation pack + recommended next steps

Hi Lena — thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap plus a small evaluation pack attached so your engineers can start running representative tests.

Key takeaways from our call:
- Goal: Improve semantic search relevance for short queries (3–8 tokens) while keeping query latency <= 120ms p95 for 4k QPS baseline.
- Data: 60M documents, average doc length ~400 tokens, host in us-west.
- Constraints: Must stay in single-region (no cross-region calls) and preserve PII handling — we discussed Private deployment options.

What we attached / shared:
- searchly_benchmark_summary_20260910.pdf — Redwood-verified performance profiles (summary TPS/P50/P95 across model variants).
- searchly_promptset_v3.json — small prompt set + exemplar queries we used in the bench.
- redwood_verified_profiles_searchly.csv — per-model numeric profile (tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency at 1, 4, 8 concurrent shards).

Top model recommendations (based on your accuracy vs latency trade-off):
1) rw-fermion-search-7B-quant (recommended for canary) — 88.2% hits@10 on your eval set; p50=45ms, p95=110ms (single GPU, 4kQPS projected w/ batching). TPS (tokens/sec) effective: 1,900 with continuous batching.
2) rw-neutron-13B-int8 (higher quality, heavier) — 92.6% hits@10; p50=78ms, p95=170ms (requires larger reserved capacity or Dedicated). TPS: 1,100.
3) fallback rw-micro-3B-quant — 80.1% hits@10; p50=30ms, p95=95ms (good for bursty low-latency requests). TPS: 3,200.

Notes on the profiles: numbers above are Redwood-verified under our standard bench harness (short query mix, synthetic KV cache disabled). The attached CSV has per-model percentile curves and shard scaling guidance. You'll see p95 moves higher with smaller batch windows or without prefix caching — we called this out in the summary.

Recommended next steps:
1) Your team picks a canary (we suggest rw-fermion-search-7B-quant) and we provide a pre-configured container with the prompt set and a short test harness.
2) Run the prompt set (attached) against a 1M sample — copy results to the Drive link and we’ll run diff/eval to flag regression patterns.
3) If latency meets your SLOs, we can propose a Dedicated configuration (reserved GPU pools) and produce a preliminary cost estimate & SOW.

Please find the benchmark links above and let me know which canary you'd like. I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through for your infra folks next week.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Ben — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick questions:
- Can you include the prompt examples as plain text too? Our infra team prefers to eyeball them before running. (I see the JSON but a short human-friendly doc helps.)
- Do the p95 numbers assume KV cache enabled? We have a warm cache for frequent queries.
- Procurement looped in — can you provide an initial pricing ballpark for the two configurations (canary: fermion-7B-quant; production: neutron-13B-int8)?

We'll try to run the prompt set Friday EOD; procurement will follow with a short vendor packet request.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Park | Head of Search, Searchly
Lena.Park@searchly.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@searchly.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Searchly evaluation pack + recommended next steps

Hi Lena — I pulled a short, plain-text prompt doc and attached it to the Drive link (also included in the summary PDF). Quick clarifications: 
- The p95s Ben quoted were from runs with Redis-style prefix caching disabled (to show worst-case cold-path). With your warm cache profile we typically see p95 ~ 20–35% lower depending on cache hit distribution — see "cache-adjusted" column in the CSV.
- The fermion-7B-quant numbers assume 4-token prompting overhead (short queries) and continuous batching with a 10ms batching window. If you reduce the batching window to prioritize tail latency, p95 will increase ~10–40ms depending on load.

I've added a recommended canary config to the Drive doc (shard count = 3, batch window = 10ms, prefix cache enabled for frequent queries). That config should get you under your 120ms p95 target in most traffic profiles.

Next actions from Redwood:
- We'll provision a time-limited test endpoint for fermion-7B-quant (no charge, 7 days) with the prompt set preloaded.
- If you'd like, we'll run an internal overlay evaluation comparing your sample results to baseline quality and flag top-10 regression queries.

Ben — can you attach the quick pricing sketch for canary vs. production (very high level) so procurement has something to review?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@searchly.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Searchly evaluation pack + recommended next steps

Adding a few throughput/ops notes for your infra team: 
- At estimated QPS mix (4k short-query QPS, avg 5 tokens per request), fermion-7B-quant at shard=3 with prefix caching should sustain ~3.8k qps with expected p50 ~48ms and p95 ~115ms. Effective token throughput (end-to-end) ~1,800 tokens/sec per shard.
- If you plan to burst + guarantee SLO, reserve one extra shard for headroom (we recommend Dedicated reserved_capacity=4). That keeps the p95 headroom under 140ms at 95th percentile traffic spikes.
- For neutron-13B-int8, plan for ~2x GPU memory and ~0.6x TPS per GPU; reasonable production sizing for 4kQPS is reserved_capacity=6 (cost estimate in sketch).

I'll prepare a short test plan (load profile + success criteria) and drop it into the Drive link by EOD.

— Jonas

1) Please activate the 7-day test endpoint and share credentials + an onboarding doc for infra.
2) Send the high-level pricing sketch so procurement can start a rough TCO.

If we can get the test endpoint and pricing sketch today, our engineers will start the promptset run this afternoon. After that, we'll sync for a short tech review.

Thanks — Lena
